jobs.title: Director, Client Enablement Analytics
jobs.description:
BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full-service financial services provider. We offer corporate and investment banking, treasury management, as well as research and advisory services to clients around the world. #bmocapitalmarkets

Mandate:

We are looking for an individual who has built out a metrics and reporting program for a client onboarding function that enabled removing bottlenecks and unlocking revenue.

The Client Enablement team is responsible for onboarding new clients and enabling them to successfully transact quickly and accurately, with high-touch service both internally and externally. The Client onboarding process encompasses Intake, Regulatory/Jurisdictional/Product Approval Compliance, Trade Reporting Compliance, Credit Line Setup, Legal Agreement (e.g. ISDA) Negotiation, Account Opening, and Electronic Setups. The group fulfills key governance requirements and plays a central role in how quickly and effectively clients are onboarded and enabled to transact with BMO Capital Markets.

Reporting to the Managing Director & Head of Client Onboarding, Client Tax Governance, and Client Operations, the Director is a senior leader who will build and lead the onboarding analytics and reporting agenda for Capital Markets, bringing a proven track record of turning operational data into commercial insight in this space. The role links client onboarding and client enablement processes to revenue, connecting onboarding milestones such as KYC, legal documentation, credit, and account set-up to client activation and revenue outcomes, and delivers the insights needed to speed up and improve the end-to-end client experience. The role will also report on selected cross sell analytics. The Data and Analytics team aggregates data from across Capital Markets systems into outcome-driven visualizations and reporting that drive insights, enable day-to-day evidence-based decision making, and support targeting for increased revenue generation.

This role will:

Working with senior leadership, set the vision and roadmap for onboarding and client enablement analytics, defining the metrics, KPIs, and reporting that matter most to senior business and operations leaders.
Provide hands-on leadership of a small team as people manager while building reports.
Link onboarding and client enablement processes to revenue, quantifying the commercial impact of cycle time, bottlenecks, and backlog on client activation and revenue realization.
Deliver insights that accelerate onboarding, reduce friction for clients and Front Office partners, and prioritize process, data, and technology improvements.
Lead stakeholder engagement with senior leaders across Front Office, Operations, AML/KYC, Legal, and Technology, translating business questions into automated reporting and data visualizations.
Provide data analytics, data governance, and data tools and technology leadership that will support Capital Markets, Client Enablement, and strategic transformation initiatives.

Key Accountabilities:

Lead the onboarding analytics and reporting strategy, establishing an end-to-end view of the client onboarding and client enablement lifecycle from client request through account activation.
Build and maintain an onboarding-to-revenue framework that links onboarding milestones (KYC, legal documentation, credit, and new accounts) to client activation, trading activity, and revenue.
Define, capture, measure, and report KPIs and SLAs (e.g., cycle time, aging, backlog, throughput, and first-time-right) that support defined business objectives.
Deliver executive-ready dashboards and data visualizations that provide actionable insights to senior business partners and governance forums.
Use data to identify bottlenecks, root causes, and improvement opportunities, and recommend solutions that speed up and improve onboarding and the client experience.
Partner with senior stakeholders to lead requirements gathering, with a focus on delivering desired business outcomes.
Provide subject matter and technical leadership in data profiling and analysis that supports Client Data Strategy and enterprise initiatives.
Champion data governance so that data is fit for purpose and meets business, usability, and data quality requirements and standards.
Drive the maturation of operational process efficiencies using automation, AI, and technology.
Mentor and develop analytics talent, fostering a culture of curiosity, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Ensure adherence to BMO privacy and confidentiality requirements (legal, compliance and operational risk).

Authorities:

Accountable for the onboarding analytics and reporting roadmap, including prioritization of reporting and insight requests.
Accountable for defining and governing onboarding KPIs, metric definitions, and the onboarding-to-revenue methodology.
Responsible for providing insightful data visualizations and executive reporting.
Responsible for BAU oversight; ensuring reports are built and breaks/issues with existing reports and/or processes are addressed in a timely manner.
Make recommendations on, and lead implementation of, process automations and improvements.

Scope & Impact:

This role has direct or indirect impact on the following:

Client Onboarding
AML/KYC
New Accounts
Legal
Tax Operations
Front Office groups
Client Enablement and client experience
Data Governance

Cross Functional Relationships:

Lines of business in Capital Markets (Global Markets and I&CB)

Front Office coverage and sales leadership; Business Management and Finance (revenue and client activity data)

Capital Markets Client Static Data, Client Onboarding, KYC/AML

Operations: Middle and Back Office teams

Corporate Support: Compliance, Legal, Technology

Knowledge & Skills:

Knowledge:

Completion of an applicable university degree and/or relevant professional designation is required.
10+ years of data, analytics, and reporting experience within the financial services industry, including progressive leadership responsibility (Data Visualization, Data Analysis & Profiling, Reference & Master Data).
Proven track record of building analytics and reporting capabilities that link operational processes to revenue and business outcomes.
Strong understanding of Capital Markets client onboarding, KYC/AML, legal documentation, credit, and account set-up processes.
Experience leading business process automation and transformation initiatives.
Solid understanding of data management practices (data visualization, data analysis, data profiling, matching, cleansing, mastering, and exception management).

Skills:

Proven ability to translate complex data into clear, executive-ready insights and recommendations that drive decisions.
Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills with senior leaders across business lines.
Experience with analyzing and manipulating data sets using data analytics tools and technologies.
Experience applying AI tools (e.g., Copilot) to analytics and reporting.
Experience using a variety of reporting and analytics tools (e.g., Power BI, DAX, M, Python, Splunk, Dataiku, Databases)
Excellent communication skills – written and verbal, including presenting to senior executives.
Ability to maintain strong attention to detail while meeting deadlines.
Collaborative leader who demonstrates initiative, is proactive, and client-focused.
Strong troubleshooting, analysis and problem-solving skills.
Proven ability to collaborate and build strong relationships with colleagues across business lines.

Working Conditions:

This role operates within an office environment with minimal exposure to discomfort or risk of ill health.

Fast paced and dynamic – work to deadlines.

Manage multiple tasks and work streams concurrently.

Salary:

The salary range for this role is $150,000 up to $170,000 CAD (subject to the candidate meeting the specific skills, experience, education, and qualification requirements)

jobs.title: Director-Technology-Infrastructure & Implementation
jobs.description:
Titre :
Directeur(-trice), Technologie, infrastructure et mise en œuvre

Lieu de travail :
Partiellement virtuel/hybride (Canada)

Type d’emploi :
Permanent à temps plein

La Croix-Rouge canadienne, organisation sans but lucratif des plus réputées et inspirantes au monde, vient en aide aux personnes et aux communautés dans le besoin au Canada et partout dans le monde et leur donne les moyens de renforcer leur résilience. À titre d’organisation figurant au palmarès des Meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026
, elle s’engage à offrir un milieu de travail accessible, diversifié, inclusif et sans obstacle.

Relevant de la direction principale, Planification et activités philanthropiques, au sein du service de Philanthropie de la Croix-Rouge canadienne, la personne retenue assurera un leadership stratégique en vue de créer l’écosystème de technologies et de données du service. En s’appuyant sur les travaux fondamentaux réalisés jusqu’à maintenant, elle supervisera l’évolution continue des systèmes, des outils et des structures de gouvernance propres au service afin de concrétiser les objectifs de croissance des revenus du service de Philanthropie.

Elle dirigera les équipes responsables de l'analyse des systèmes opérationnels et du développement Web; à cette fin, elle définira l'orientation stratégique et opérationnelle et veillera au respect des priorités du service. Elle travaillera également en étroite collaboration avec la direction du service de Philanthropie, et d’autres unités opérationnelles (Groupe technologique, Finances), afin d’arrimer la stratégie et la gouvernance en matière de technologies et de données avec les besoins opérationnels.

Enfin, elle se tiendra au courant des tendances du domaine pour mettre à profit l’intelligence artificielle et les technologies émergentes, tout en veillant à faire évoluer continuellement la feuille de route technologique afin de faire progresser les priorités stratégiques du service de Philanthropie.

Tâches et responsabilités

Diriger et encadrer les équipes responsables de l’analyse des systèmes opérationnels et du développement Web, en définissant les orientations, en renforçant les capacités grâce à la planification du perfectionnement et des effectifs, et en accompagnant les membres des équipes dans leur développement de carrière.
Définir l'orientation stratégique et opérationnelle de l'écosystème de technologies et de données du service de Philanthropie, en traduisant les priorités en feuilles de route et plans concrets.
Agir à titre d’administratrice ou d’administrateur des données au sein du service de Philanthropie, en mettant en place une structure de gouvernance encadrant l’utilisation des données et des technologies, ainsi que la gestion des processus et des produits, conformément aux normes de gouvernance de l’organisation.
Collaborer avec la direction du Groupe technologique, du service des Finances et d’autres équipes au sein du service de Philanthropie afin d’arrimer la stratégie technologique, les normes et la gouvernance avec les besoins opérationnels changeants.
Diriger la gestion du changement dans le cadre d’initiatives technologiques et opérationnelles, en anticipant les points de résistance, en favorisant l’adhésion et en assurant l’adoption.
Gérer le budget ainsi que les relations avec les fournisseurs, en veillant à la reddition de comptes et au rendement des investissements technologiques du service.
Élaborer des dossiers d’analyse et les présenter à la haute direction afin d’obtenir le financement, les ressources et le soutien de l’organisation nécessaires à la réalisation des initiatives clés.
Se tenir à l’affût des tendances du secteur et des technologies émergentes, notamment l’intelligence artificielle, en adaptant des stratégies pertinentes afin de soutenir la croissance des revenus et l’atteinte des priorités stratégiques du service de Philanthropie.
Établir et mettre à jour les pratiques exemplaires, les normes et les cadres de gouvernance qui renforcent la maturité en matière de données et de technologies à l'échelle du service.
Cerner, évaluer et atténuer les risques liés aux opérations ou aux systèmes, en veillant à la mise en place de pratiques appropriées en matière de gouvernance et de conformité.

Profil recherché

Posséder au moins de 8 à 12 ans d'expérience professionnelle pertinente ou une combinaison équivalente d'études et d'expérience en administration des affaires, en développement des affaires, en opérations, en analyse des données, en gestion de l'information ou dans un domaine pertinent, y compris de 5 à 7 ans d'expérience en gestion de personnel en ayant démontré sa capacité à diriger des équipes dans le cadre de changements et de transformations organisationnelles.
Posséder une expérience professionnelle dans le secteur sans but lucratif constitue un atout considérable; la connaissance du marketing, de la collecte de fonds ou de la vente constitue un atout.
Pouvoir conceptualiser et harmoniser des stratégies et les concrétiser en plans opérationnels complets et cohérents qui permettent de rapprocher les tâches quotidiennes des objectifs opérationnels du service de Philanthropie.
Pouvoir synthétiser des renseignements complexes et les communiquer à divers groupes de parties prenantes, en ayant de solides compétences en matière de persuasion, de négociation et de recherche de consensus.
Avoir prouvé sa capacité à planifier et à réaliser des projets de transformation technologique, organisationnelle ou en matière de données de moyenne à grande envergure.
Avoir une grande compréhension des systèmes de gestion des relations avec la clientèle (CRM) et des technologies plus générales liées à la collecte de fonds ou au marketing numérique (p. ex. plateformes de dons, outils de marketing par courriel et par message texte, traitement des dons).
Posséder une bonne connaissance du cadre réglementaire applicable au secteur caritatif canadien en matière de traitement des données, notamment la protection des données et de la vie privée, le consentement à la communication de renseignements et les obligations de conservation de dossiers à des fins fiscales (LPRPDE, LCAP, norme de l’ICP, ARC, etc.)
Pouvoir travailler efficacement dans un environnement complexe aux priorités multiples et parfois conflictuelles.
Avoir de l’expérience en gestion de budgets et de relations avec les fournisseurs.
Maîtriser les applications de base de la suite Microsoft Office.
Maîtriser l’anglais à l’oral et à l’écrit; la maîtrise du français constitue un atout.

Conditions de travail

La personne travaille selon un modèle hybride prévoyant une combinaison de travail en personne et à distance.
Le travail se déroule dans un environnement en évolution rapide où les priorités et les échéances changent souvent.
Il implique d’interagir avec des parties prenantes dans des situations délicates ou très stressantes.
Il exige un souci du détail, une grande concentration et la capacité de traiter une importante quantité d’informations.
Il exige de s’adapter à des changements dans l’ordre des priorités, de prendre des décisions sous pression et de parvenir à effectuer ses tâches à un rythme imprévisible.
Il exige le respect de multiples échéances conflictuelles.
L’emploi prévoit des déplacements dans des zones sûres, mais pourrait parfois contraindre la personne à évoluer dans des conditions difficiles.
Étant donné que nous offrons des services à des communautés et que nous travaillons avec des personnes (gestionnaires, collègues, clientèles, bénévoles, bailleurs de fonds et partenaires externes) partout au Canada et dans le monde, la personne retenue pourrait devoir assumer les responsabilités de son poste en anglais même s’il ne s’agit pas de sa langue maternelle.
Admissibilité à travailler au Canada : Nous invitons toutes les personnes qualifiées qui peuvent être employées au Canada à présenter leur candidature. Les personnes qui n’ont pas la citoyenneté ou la résidence permanente du Canada sont encouragées à examiner attentivement leur visa pour savoir si elles sont en mesure d’occuper le poste pour lequel elles présentent leur candidature. Pour obtenir de plus amples renseignements, veuillez consulter notre Foire aux questions.
La personne retenue devra réussir le processus de présélection et accepter de se soumettre à une vérification approfondie des antécédents judiciaires.

jobs.title: Director, I&IT Data Platform & Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Description

Metrolinx is connecting communities across the Greater Golden Horseshoe. Metrolinx operates GO Transit and UP Express, as well as the PRESTO fare payment system. We are also building new and improved rapid transit, including GO Expansion, Light Rail Transit routes, and major expansions to Toronto’s subway system, to get people where they need to go, better, faster and easier. Metrolinx is an agency of the Government of Ontario.

At Metrolinx, equity, diversity and inclusion are essential to living our values of serving with passion, thinking forward and playing as a team.

Metrolinx's Innovation and Information Technology group supports female team members via "Go Tech Women" an affinity group for women in Information Technology, led by our Chief Information Officer.

If you enjoy technology and innovation, value diversity, appreciate work/balance and are looking for an opportunity to make a better world via public service, Metrolinx would like to hear from you!

Reporting to the VP, I&IT Enterprise AI & Data Centre of Excellence, the Director, Enterprise Data Platform & Engineering is accountable for the strategy, engineering, delivery and operation of Metrolinx's enterprise data platform and the trusted data foundation that enables analytics, artificial intelligence and data-driven decision-making across the organization.

The Director leads the modernization and evolution of Metrolinx's enterprise data platform, including cloud data infrastructure, data lake/lakehouse capabilities, data engineering, integration, DataOps and platform services. The role is accountable for establishing scalable, secure and reusable platform capabilities based on a "build once, reuse many times" approach, enabling business units to access trusted data and deliver data and AI products more efficiently.

Working within a federated operating model where business areas retain accountability for their data and business outcomes, the Director partners with business leaders, I&IT, Enterprise Architecture, Data Governance, Cybersecurity, AI teams and strategic vendors to ensure enterprise data capabilities are secure, governed, interoperable, cost-effective and aligned with Metrolinx's Enterprise Data and AI strategies.

The Director also provides leadership to multidisciplinary engineering teams and strategic partners, establishing modern engineering practices, platform standards and delivery disciplines while building the organizational capabilities required to scale data and AI across Metrolinx.

What will I be doing?

Strategy and leadership: Develop and operationalize Metrolinx's Enterprise Data Platform strategy and roadmap, translating the Enterprise Data and AI strategies into platform capabilities, investment priorities and measurable maturity targets.
Platform ownership: Own the enterprise data platform as a strategic enterprise capability, including its architecture, engineering, scalability, performance, reliability, lifecycle and ongoing evolution.
Data platform modernization: Lead the modernization of Metrolinx's data environment toward a scalable, cloud-native and AI-ready architecture, evolving data lake and related capabilities into a modern enterprise data platform that supports analytics, reporting, machine learning, generative AI and enterprise data products.
Data engineering: Establish and lead enterprise data engineering capabilities, including ingestion, integration, transformation, orchestration and reusable data pipelines, enabling trusted data to move efficiently from source systems into enterprise analytical and AI environments.
Engineering excellence: Establish engineering standards and practices for DataOps, DevOps, CI/CD, Infrastructure-as-Code, automated testing, observability, monitoring and release management to improve the quality, speed and reliability of data platform delivery.
AI-ready data foundation: Partner with AI teams to ensure enterprise data and platform capabilities can securely support machine learning, advanced analytics and generative AI use cases, including appropriate data access, integration, scalability, governance and operational controls.
Reusable data capabilities: Establish common enterprise data services, patterns and reusable components that reduce duplication and accelerate the delivery of data, analytics and AI solutions across Metrolinx.
Delivery management: Deliver projects on scope, on time and on budget, using a Lean Agile approach with clear milestones. Work with Scrum Masters, Product Owners and vendors to prioritize software work and keep quality high.
Enterprise data architecture: Own and evolve Metrolinx's enterprise data architecture, including target-state architecture, standards, principles, patterns and roadmaps. Establish architectural guardrails for data platforms, integration, storage, data movement and data products to enable interoperability, reuse and scalability across the enterprise. Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Cybersecurity, Data Governance and business technology teams to ensure data solutions align with broader enterprise architecture and technology strategies.
Architecture governance: Establish and oversee data architecture governance to ensure new solutions and investments align with enterprise data standards and target-state architecture, reducing duplication, technical debt and unnecessary point-to-point integration.
Executive communication: Run strategic workshops with the business to define goals and requirements. Prepare regular updates for the CIO, CFO and executive team. Handle escalations with solutions ready.
Stakeholder partnerships: Build trusted relationships at executive and working levels with internal teams, vendors, partners, government and agencies. Act as a Metrolinx ambassador in public presentations and meetings.
Financial stewardship: Own annual and long-term budgets, staffing plans and ROI. Put in place the controls and reporting for cost management. Hold signing authority within the role's scope.
People leadership: Lead a large department through subordinate supervisors. Set clear roles and expectations, give timely feedback and address performance gaps. Build a "best company to work for" culture.
Talent and vendor scale-up: Work with other senior technology leaders to scale a 50+ member team of internal and external resources across multiple geographies. Keep the talent and vendor mix right. Mentor talent in line with future I&IT strategy.

What Skills and Qualifications Do I Need?

Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data/Information Management or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education, training and senior-level experience.
Significant leadership experience building and operating enterprise-scale data platforms, data engineering capabilities and cloud data environments within a complex organization.
Strong knowledge of modern data-platform architectures, including cloud data platforms, data lakes/lakehouses, data warehousing, data integration, APIs and distributed data-processing patterns.
Demonstrated experience modernizing legacy data environments and establishing cloud-native, scalable and reusable data-platform capabilities.
Strong understanding of Microsoft Azure data technologies and contemporary platforms such as Azure Databricks and Microsoft Fabric, or comparable enterprise technologies.
Experience establishing DataOps/DevOps practices, CI/CD, Infrastructure-as-Code, automated testing, observability and production engineering standards.
Demonstrated experience enabling enterprise analytics, machine learning and generative AI workloads through well-governed and scalable data platforms.
Strong knowledge of enterprise data governance, data quality, metadata, master/reference data, security, privacy and lifecycle management, and the ability to translate these requirements into platform capabilities.
Experience operating within a federated data model, enabling business-owned data products while maintaining enterprise standards, interoperability and governance.
Demonstrated experience leading large multidisciplinary teams and strategic vendors across onshore, offshore and/or nearshore delivery models.
Strong financial management experience, including cloud consumption management, technology investment planning, vendor management and platform FinOps.
Proven ability to translate complex technical issues into clear recommendations and communicate credibly with CIO/CFO/executive-level stakeholders.
Strong understanding of Agile product and platform delivery models and experience managing enterprise technology portfolios involving multiple business units and dependencies.

Don’t Meet Every Requirement?

If you’re excited about working with Metrolinx but your past experience doesn’t quite align with every qualification of this posting, we encourage you to apply. You just might be the right candidate for this or other roles. We are always looking for great talent to join our team.

We invite all interested individuals to apply and encourage applications from members of equity-deserving communities, including those who identify as Indigenous, Black, racialized, women, people with disabilities, and people with diverse gender identities, expressions and sexual orientations.

Accommodation

Metrolinx is an equal opportunity employer and committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce. We are also committed to offering reasonable accommodation to job applicants in accordance with applicable legislation. If you require assistance or an accommodation at any point during the hiring process, please contact us at: 416-202-5601 or email hr.recruitment@metrolinx.com.

Application Process

All applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada. Metrolinx will be using email to communicate with you for all job competitions. It is your responsibility to include an updated email address that is checked daily and accepts emails from unknown users. As we send time-sensitive correspondence, we recommend that you check your email regularly. If no response is received, we will assume you are no longer interested in pursuing the opportunity. Please be advised that a Criminal Record Check may be required of the successful candidate.

jobs.title: Director, AI & Automation – Supply Chain
jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

The Director, AI & Automation is a senior business transformation leader accountable for setting the direction for, and leading the identification, prioritization, and delivery of, artificial intelligence, generative AI, intelligent automation, and digital workflow solutions across Procurement and the broader Operations organization. The role will translate enterprise and business priorities into a scalable portfolio of initiatives that simplify work, improve decision-making, strengthen controls, and create measurable operational and financial value.

Working under DIO-centered governance and in continuous partnership with DIO leadership and the DIO organizations, this role will own the business AI and automation roadmap and lead business initiatives from discovery and business-case development through solution design, deployment, adoption, and value realization. No AI or automation initiative will advance outside established DIO engagement, intake, architecture, platform, data, Information Security, and Cybersecurity processes. The Director will connect business process expertise with approved enterprise platforms and technical capabilities, including AI assistants and agents, machine learning, robotic process automation, workflow automation, intelligent document processing, process mining, analytics, and low-code solutions.

The role will serve as a strategic partner to Procurement, MCE, GDC, and other Operations senior leaders, leading the redesign of priority processes and scaling practical solutions that reduce manual effort, cycle time, cost, and operational risk. All opportunities, experiments, pilots, and production deployments will be planned and executed with DIO engagement and in alignment with enterprise architecture, Information Security, Cybersecurity, privacy, data governance, Responsible AI, and change-management requirements

Responsibilities

AI & Automation Strategy and Portfolio

Set the vision for and own a multi-year AI and automation roadmap aligned with Procurement, MCE, GDC, and broader Operations priorities
Partner with DIO leadership to apply its established intake and assessment process to identify, size, prioritize, and sequence opportunities based on business value, feasibility, risk, data readiness, security requirements, and scalability
Own business cases, delivery plans, resource requirements, investment asks, and benefit targets for the portfolio, with clear accountability and executive decision points
Monitor market and enterprise technology developments and advise senior leadership on practical use cases that address defined business problems rather than technology-driven experimentation

Business Partnership and Process Transformation

Serve as a trusted advisor to Procurement and Operations leaders to shape strategic priorities, map end-to-end processes, identify root causes, and redesign work before automating it
Direct focus toward high-value opportunities across source-to-pay, supplier management, contracting, risk and compliance, planning, project delivery, asset operations, and shared operational services
Partner with MCE and GDC leadership to improve productivity, throughput, service levels, data quality, cost performance, and execution predictability

About The Role

North Vector Dynamics is building next-generation defence systems, and we’re scaling fast: from prototype builds to production, from a handful of people to a full team, and through our next stages of growth and financing. We’re looking for a Director of Finance to build the finance function behind it: the planning, reporting, controls, and capital strategy that let us make good decisions quickly and prove to investors, customers, and auditors that we can be trusted with their money. Reporting to the CEO directly, you’ll own our budget, forecast, and cash runway, run month-end and year-end, and turn our books into the numbers leadership and the board steer by.

This is a ground-floor role for someone who is rigorous, commercially minded, and energized by building systems from a clean sheet rather than inheriting them. You’ll work side by side with every department head, our bookkeeping and accounting support, our investors and board, and senior leadership, and your work will shape how far and how fast this company can grow.

If you want to build the financial foundation for a company whose platforms will one day support operators in the field, save lives, and serve sovereign national interest - this role was written for you.

What You’ll Do

Financial Planning & Analysis

Own the annual budget and rolling forecast: setting up cost centers, building department budgets with each head, and reporting budget-to-actual variances every month.
Build and maintain the company financial model and cash runway, modelling hiring plans, capital spending (including our new manufacturing facility), and program scenarios so leadership can see the trade-offs before committing.
Produce monthly management reporting for leadership and the board: P&L by cost center, burn, runway, program costs, and the KPIs that tell us whether we’re on track.

Accounting, Controls & Compliance

Own month-end and year-end close, the general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, and payroll oversight, building on our current bookkeeping foundation and growing the accounting team as we scale.
Design the internal controls a defence supplier is held to: approval authorities, purchasing and expense policies, segregation of duties, and an audit trail that holds up to scrutiny.
Manage our annual financial statement audit or review, corporate income tax, GST, and claims under SR&ED and other government incentive programs.
Lead program and contract finance: cost estimating and pricing support for bids, milestone billing, revenue recognition, and contract cost accounting that meets Government of Canada and allied customer requirements.

Capital, Investors & Systems

Support fundraising and investor relations: board and investor reporting, data rooms, and financial due diligence for future rounds, and manage the cap table and equity plan administration with legal counsel.
Find, secure and manage non-dilutive funding: government grants, contribution programs, and innovation funding that extend our runway.
Run treasury and banking: cash management, foreign exchange for international suppliers, credit facilities, and corporate insurance.
Lead the finance side of our ERP selection and rollout: chart of accounts, cost-center structure, and clean integration with purchasing, inventory, and manufacturing.
Step into whatever the mission demands: this is a startup, and no two weeks will look the same.

Required

What You Bring

A CPA designation (or similar) in good standing, with a degree in accounting, finance, or business.
10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including at least 3 years leading a finance function or team, ideally in a manufacturing or hardware company.
Hands-on FP&A experience: building budgets, forecasts, and three-statement financial models from scratch, and presenting them clearly to non-finance leaders.
Deep experience with month-end close, financial reporting under ASPE or IFRS, external audits, and Canadian corporate tax.
Experience supporting a venture-backed or high-growth company through financing rounds, board reporting, and investor due diligence.
A track record of standing up accounting systems, internal controls, and policies that scaled with the business.
Eligibility for a Government of Canada security clearance and registration under the Controlled Goods Program; active clearance is a significant asset.
A builder’s mindset: you take ownership of the system, not just the task, and you’re as comfortable building a model at midnight before a board meeting as you are designing the process that makes it unnecessary next time.

Preferred

Experience in a defence or aerospace company, including government contract costing, pricing, and audit (Public Services and Procurement Canada, DND, or US DoD contracts).
Experience preparing SR&ED claims and managing IRAP, IDEaS, or similar non-dilutive funding programs.
Manufacturing cost accounting experience: standard costing, inventory valuation, work in progress, and cost of goods sold.
Experience with Series B or later financings, venture debt, or other growth capital.
Experience with equity plan administration and cap table tools such as Carta.
Multi-entity or international experience: US or European subsidiaries, foreign exchange, and transfer pricing.

Why North Vector Dynamics

Real ownership from day one: the systems and processes you help build will be foundational to how this company operates for years to come.
We’re working on technology that matters at a national and global level, and every person on the team feels that weight and that purpose.
A tight-knit, high-calibre team that moves fast, holds each other to a high standard, and doesn’t waste time on bureaucracy for its own sake.
Competitive compensation and meaningful upside from joining an early-stage company at the forefront of the defence technology sector.

La Croix-Rouge canadienne, organisation sans but lucratif des plus réputées et inspirantes au monde, vient en aide aux personnes et aux communautés dans le besoin au Canada et partout dans le monde et leur donne les moyens de renforcer leur résilience. À titre d’organisation figurant au palmarès des Meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026
, elle s’engage à offrir un milieu de travail accessible, diversifié, inclusif et sans obstacle.

Relevant de la direction principale, Planification et activités philanthropiques, au sein du service de Philanthropie de la Croix-Rouge canadienne, la personne retenue assurera un leadership stratégique en vue de créer l’écosystème de technologies et de données du service. En s’appuyant sur les travaux fondamentaux réalisés jusqu’à maintenant, elle supervisera l’évolution continue des systèmes, des outils et des structures de gouvernance propres au service afin de concrétiser les objectifs de croissance des revenus du service de Philanthropie.

Elle dirigera les équipes responsables de l'analyse des systèmes opérationnels et du développement Web; à cette fin, elle définira l'orientation stratégique et opérationnelle et veillera au respect des priorités du service. Elle travaillera également en étroite collaboration avec la direction du service de Philanthropie, et d’autres unités opérationnelles (Groupe technologique, Finances), afin d’arrimer la stratégie et la gouvernance en matière de technologies et de données avec les besoins opérationnels.

Enfin, elle se tiendra au courant des tendances du domaine pour mettre à profit l’intelligence artificielle et les technologies émergentes, tout en veillant à faire évoluer continuellement la feuille de route technologique afin de faire progresser les priorités stratégiques du service de Philanthropie.

Tâches et responsabilités

Diriger et encadrer les équipes responsables de l’analyse des systèmes opérationnels et du développement Web, en définissant les orientations, en renforçant les capacités grâce à la planification du perfectionnement et des effectifs, et en accompagnant les membres des équipes dans leur développement de carrière.
Définir l'orientation stratégique et opérationnelle de l'écosystème de technologies et de données du service de Philanthropie, en traduisant les priorités en feuilles de route et plans concrets.
Agir à titre d’administratrice ou d’administrateur des données au sein du service de Philanthropie, en mettant en place une structure de gouvernance encadrant l’utilisation des données et des technologies, ainsi que la gestion des processus et des produits, conformément aux normes de gouvernance de l’organisation.
Collaborer avec la direction du Groupe technologique, du service des Finances et d’autres équipes au sein du service de Philanthropie afin d’arrimer la stratégie technologique, les normes et la gouvernance avec les besoins opérationnels changeants.
Diriger la gestion du changement dans le cadre d’initiatives technologiques et opérationnelles, en anticipant les points de résistance, en favorisant l’adhésion et en assurant l’adoption.
Gérer le budget ainsi que les relations avec les fournisseurs, en veillant à la reddition de comptes et au rendement des investissements technologiques du service.
Élaborer des dossiers d’analyse et les présenter à la haute direction afin d’obtenir le financement, les ressources et le soutien de l’organisation nécessaires à la réalisation des initiatives clés.
Se tenir à l’affût des tendances du secteur et des technologies émergentes, notamment l’intelligence artificielle, en adaptant des stratégies pertinentes afin de soutenir la croissance des revenus et l’atteinte des priorités stratégiques du service de Philanthropie.
Établir et mettre à jour les pratiques exemplaires, les normes et les cadres de gouvernance qui renforcent la maturité en matière de données et de technologies à l'échelle du service.
Cerner, évaluer et atténuer les risques liés aux opérations ou aux systèmes, en veillant à la mise en place de pratiques appropriées en matière de gouvernance et de conformité.

Profil recherché

Posséder au moins de 8 à 12 ans d'expérience professionnelle pertinente ou une combinaison équivalente d'études et d'expérience en administration des affaires, en développement des affaires, en opérations, en analyse des données, en gestion de l'information ou dans un domaine pertinent, y compris de 5 à 7 ans d'expérience en gestion de personnel en ayant démontré sa capacité à diriger des équipes dans le cadre de changements et de transformations organisationnelles.
Posséder une expérience professionnelle dans le secteur sans but lucratif constitue un atout considérable; la connaissance du marketing, de la collecte de fonds ou de la vente constitue un atout.
Pouvoir conceptualiser et harmoniser des stratégies et les concrétiser en plans opérationnels complets et cohérents qui permettent de rapprocher les tâches quotidiennes des objectifs opérationnels du service de Philanthropie.
Pouvoir synthétiser des renseignements complexes et les communiquer à divers groupes de parties prenantes, en ayant de solides compétences en matière de persuasion, de négociation et de recherche de consensus.
Avoir prouvé sa capacité à planifier et à réaliser des projets de transformation technologique, organisationnelle ou en matière de données de moyenne à grande envergure.
Avoir une grande compréhension des systèmes de gestion des relations avec la clientèle (CRM) et des technologies plus générales liées à la collecte de fonds ou au marketing numérique (p. ex. plateformes de dons, outils de marketing par courriel et par message texte, traitement des dons).
Posséder une bonne connaissance du cadre réglementaire applicable au secteur caritatif canadien en matière de traitement des données, notamment la protection des données et de la vie privée, le consentement à la communication de renseignements et les obligations de conservation de dossiers à des fins fiscales (LPRPDE, LCAP, norme de l’ICP, ARC, etc.)
Pouvoir travailler efficacement dans un environnement complexe aux priorités multiples et parfois conflictuelles.
Avoir de l’expérience en gestion de budgets et de relations avec les fournisseurs.
Maîtriser les applications de base de la suite Microsoft Office.
Maîtriser l’anglais à l’oral et à l’écrit; la maîtrise du français constitue un atout.

Conditions de travail

La personne travaille selon un modèle hybride prévoyant une combinaison de travail en personne et à distance.
Le travail se déroule dans un environnement en évolution rapide où les priorités et les échéances changent souvent.
Il implique d’interagir avec des parties prenantes dans des situations délicates ou très stressantes.
Il exige un souci du détail, une grande concentration et la capacité de traiter une importante quantité d’informations.
Il exige de s’adapter à des changements dans l’ordre des priorités, de prendre des décisions sous pression et de parvenir à effectuer ses tâches à un rythme imprévisible.
Il exige le respect de multiples échéances conflictuelles.
L’emploi prévoit des déplacements dans des zones sûres, mais pourrait parfois contraindre la personne à évoluer dans des conditions difficiles.
Étant donné que nous offrons des services à des communautés et que nous travaillons avec des personnes (gestionnaires, collègues, clientèles, bénévoles, bailleurs de fonds et partenaires externes) partout au Canada et dans le monde, la personne retenue pourrait devoir assumer les responsabilités de son poste en anglais même s’il ne s’agit pas de sa langue maternelle.
Admissibilité à travailler au Canada : Nous invitons toutes les personnes qualifiées qui peuvent être employées au Canada à présenter leur candidature. Les personnes qui n’ont pas la citoyenneté ou la résidence permanente du Canada sont encouragées à examiner attentivement leur visa pour savoir si elles sont en mesure d’occuper le poste pour lequel elles présentent leur candidature. Job Description

Metrolinx is connecting communities across the Greater Golden Horseshoe. Metrolinx operates GO Transit and UP Express, as well as the PRESTO fare payment system. We are also building new and improved rapid transit, including GO Expansion, Light Rail Transit routes, and major expansions to Toronto’s subway system, to get people where they need to go, better, faster and easier. Metrolinx is an agency of the Government of Ontario.

At Metrolinx, equity, diversity and inclusion are essential to living our values of serving with passion, thinking forward and playing as a team.

Metrolinx's Innovation and Information Technology group supports female team members via "Go Tech Women" an affinity group for women in Information Technology, led by our Chief Information Officer.

If you enjoy technology and innovation, value diversity, appreciate work/balance and are looking for an opportunity to make a better world via public service, Metrolinx would like to hear from you!

Reporting to the VP, I&IT Enterprise AI & Data Centre of Excellence, the Director, Enterprise Data Platform & Engineering is accountable for the strategy, engineering, delivery and operation of Metrolinx's enterprise data platform and the trusted data foundation that enables analytics, artificial intelligence and data-driven decision-making across the organization.

The Director leads the modernization and evolution of Metrolinx's enterprise data platform, including cloud data infrastructure, data lake/lakehouse capabilities, data engineering, integration, DataOps and platform services. The role is accountable for establishing scalable, secure and reusable platform capabilities based on a "build once, reuse many times" approach, enabling business units to access trusted data and deliver data and AI products more efficiently.

Working within a federated operating model where business areas retain accountability for their data and business outcomes, the Director partners with business leaders, I&IT, Enterprise Architecture, Data Governance, Cybersecurity, AI teams and strategic vendors to ensure enterprise data capabilities are secure, governed, interoperable, cost-effective and aligned with Metrolinx's Enterprise Data and AI strategies.

The Director also provides leadership to multidisciplinary engineering teams and strategic partners, establishing modern engineering practices, platform standards and delivery disciplines while building the organizational capabilities required to scale data and AI across Metrolinx.

What will I be doing?

Strategy and leadership: Develop and operationalize Metrolinx's Enterprise Data Platform strategy and roadmap, translating the Enterprise Data and AI strategies into platform capabilities, investment priorities and measurable maturity targets.
Platform ownership: Own the enterprise data platform as a strategic enterprise capability, including its architecture, engineering, scalability, performance, reliability, lifecycle and ongoing evolution.
Data platform modernization: Lead the modernization of Metrolinx's data environment toward a scalable, cloud-native and AI-ready architecture, evolving data lake and related capabilities into a modern enterprise data platform that supports analytics, reporting, machine learning, generative AI and enterprise data products.
Data engineering: Establish and lead enterprise data engineering capabilities, including ingestion, integration, transformation, orchestration and reusable data pipelines, enabling trusted data to move efficiently from source systems into enterprise analytical and AI environments.
Engineering excellence: Establish engineering standards and practices for DataOps, DevOps, CI/CD, Infrastructure-as-Code, automated testing, observability, monitoring and release management to improve the quality, speed and reliability of data platform delivery.
AI-ready data foundation: Partner with AI teams to ensure enterprise data and platform capabilities can securely support machine learning, advanced analytics and generative AI use cases, including appropriate data access, integration, scalability, governance and operational controls.
Reusable data capabilities: Establish common enterprise data services, patterns and reusable components that reduce duplication and accelerate the delivery of data, analytics and AI solutions across Metrolinx.
Delivery management: Deliver projects on scope, on time and on budget, using a Lean Agile approach with clear milestones. Work with Scrum Masters, Product Owners and vendors to prioritize software work and keep quality high.
Enterprise data architecture: Own and evolve Metrolinx's enterprise data architecture, including target-state architecture, standards, principles, patterns and roadmaps. Establish architectural guardrails for data platforms, integration, storage, data movement and data products to enable interoperability, reuse and scalability across the enterprise. Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Cybersecurity, Data Governance and business technology teams to ensure data solutions align with broader enterprise architecture and technology strategies.
Architecture governance: Establish and oversee data architecture governance to ensure new solutions and investments align with enterprise data standards and target-state architecture, reducing duplication, technical debt and unnecessary point-to-point integration.
Executive communication: Run strategic workshops with the business to define goals and requirements. Prepare regular updates for the CIO, CFO and executive team. Handle escalations with solutions ready.
Stakeholder partnerships: Build trusted relationships at executive and working levels with internal teams, vendors, partners, government and agencies. Act as a Metrolinx ambassador in public presentations and meetings.
Financial stewardship: Own annual and long-term budgets, staffing plans and ROI. Put in place the controls and reporting for cost management. Hold signing authority within the role's scope.
People leadership: Lead a large department through subordinate supervisors. Set clear roles and expectations, give timely feedback and address performance gaps. Build a "best company to work for" culture.
Talent and vendor scale-up: Work with other senior technology leaders to scale a 50+ member team of internal and external resources across multiple geographies. Keep the talent and vendor mix right. Mentor talent in line with future I&IT strategy.

What Skills and Qualifications Do I Need?

Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data/Information Management or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education, training and senior-level experience.
Significant leadership experience building and operating enterprise-scale data platforms, data engineering capabilities and cloud data environments within a complex organization.
Strong knowledge of modern data-platform architectures, including cloud data platforms, data lakes/lakehouses, data warehousing, data integration, APIs and distributed data-processing patterns.
Demonstrated experience modernizing legacy data environments and establishing cloud-native, scalable and reusable data-platform capabilities.
Strong understanding of Microsoft Azure data technologies and contemporary platforms such as Azure Databricks and Microsoft Fabric, or comparable enterprise technologies.
Experience establishing DataOps/DevOps practices, CI/CD, Infrastructure-as-Code, automated testing, observability and production engineering standards.
Demonstrated experience enabling enterprise analytics, machine learning and generative AI workloads through well-governed and scalable data platforms.
Strong knowledge of enterprise data governance, data quality, metadata, master/reference data, security, privacy and lifecycle management, and the ability to translate these requirements into platform capabilities.
Experience operating within a federated data model, enabling business-owned data products while maintaining enterprise standards, interoperability and governance.
Demonstrated experience leading large multidisciplinary teams and strategic vendors across onshore, offshore and/or nearshore delivery models.
Strong financial management experience, including cloud consumption management, technology investment planning, vendor management and platform FinOps.
Proven ability to translate complex technical issues into clear recommendations and communicate credibly with CIO/CFO/executive-level stakeholders.
Strong understanding of Agile product and platform delivery models and experience managing enterprise technology portfolios involving multiple business units and dependencies.

Don’t Meet Every Requirement?

If you’re excited about working with Metrolinx but your past experience doesn’t quite align with every qualification of this posting, we encourage you to apply. You just might be the right candidate for this or other roles. We are always looking for great talent to join our team.

We invite all interested individuals to apply and encourage applications from members of equity-deserving communities, including those who identify as Indigenous, Black, racialized, women, people with disabilities, and people with diverse gender identities, expressions and sexual orientations.

About The Role

North Vector Dynamics is building next-generation defence systems, and we’re scaling fast: from prototype builds to production, from a handful of people to a full team, and through our next stages of growth and financing. We’re looking for a Director of Finance to build the finance function behind it: the planning, reporting, controls, and capital strategy that let us make good decisions quickly and prove to investors, customers, and auditors that we can be trusted with their money. Reporting to the CEO directly, you’ll own our budget, forecast, and cash runway, run month-end and year-end, and turn our books into the numbers leadership and the board steer by.

This is a ground-floor role for someone who is rigorous, commercially minded, and energized by building systems from a clean sheet rather than inheriting them. You’ll work side by side with every department head, our bookkeeping and accounting support, our investors and board, and senior leadership, and your work will shape how far and how fast this company can grow.

If you want to build the financial foundation for a company whose platforms will one day support operators in the field, save lives, and serve sovereign national interest - this role was written for you.

What You’ll Do

Financial Planning & Analysis

Own the annual budget and rolling forecast: setting up cost centers, building department budgets with each head, and reporting budget-to-actual variances every month.
Build and maintain the company financial model and cash runway, modelling hiring plans, capital spending (including our new manufacturing facility), and program scenarios so leadership can see the trade-offs before committing.
Produce monthly management reporting for leadership and the board: P&L by cost center, burn, runway, program costs, and the KPIs that tell us whether we’re on track.

Accounting, Controls & Compliance

Own month-end and year-end close, the general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, and payroll oversight, building on our current bookkeeping foundation and growing the accounting team as we scale.
Design the internal controls a defence supplier is held to: approval authorities, purchasing and expense policies, segregation of duties, and an audit trail that holds up to scrutiny.
Manage our annual financial statement audit or review, corporate income tax, GST, and claims under SR&ED and other government incentive programs.
Lead program and contract finance: cost estimating and pricing support for bids, milestone billing, revenue recognition, and contract cost accounting that meets Government of Canada and allied customer requirements.
